spec.full_target:
Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
\(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.

Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove

\[
\dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
\]

The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
spec.conclusion: dimH(G)=dimH(E)+1, where E has its original Euclidean metric and G is E×[0,1] identified with Euclidean Rn(n₀+1) as specified in the selected target; this holds for every natural n₀, including n₀=0. Both sides are finite, so the equality also holds for real Hausdorff dimensions.

definitions.type: family of Euclidean real normed spaces indexed by natural numbers
definitions.definition: For each natural m, Rn(m)=EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m), namely real m-tuples with norm (Σ_{h<m}|x_h|²)^(1/2). For m=0 this is the one-point zero vector space.

definitions.type: extended diameter of a subset of an emetric space
definitions.definition: For an emetric space W and B⊆W, ediam(B)=sup{edist(x,y):x,y∈B} in ℝ≥0∞; the empty supremum is zero.

definitions.type: real diameter of a bounded subset of a metric space
definitions.definition: For a bounded subset B of a metric space W, diam(B)=sup{dist(x,y):x,y∈B}, with diam(∅)=0. Its cast to ℝ≥0∞ is ediam(B). This notation is used only after boundedness has been established.

For an emetric space W, B⊆W, real a and r∈ℝ≥0∞, content(a,r,B)= inf_{U:ℕ→Set W} inf_{B⊆⋃i U_i} inf_{∀i ediam(U_i)≤r} Σ'_i sup_{h:U_i nonempty} ediam(U_i)^a. Infima and sums take values in ℝ≥0∞. A failed condition has empty infimum ∞; the supremum over a nonemptiness proof is zero for an empty member. This is exactly BasisObjects.content in basis-registry.json /lean_header.

For a metric space W, B⊆W, a>0 and δ>0, C^a_δ(B)=content(a,ENNReal.ofReal δ,B). The original real-diameter convention is the infimum of Σ_i diam(U_i)^a over countable covers of B with diam(U_i)≤δ, empty members contributing zero. The proof establishes compatibility of these two formulations.

binders.type: countable family of subsets of W

definitions.type: unnormalized Hausdorff measure evaluated on a set
definitions.definition: For a Borel emetric space W, B⊆W and real a, H^a(B)=MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure a B. This is the metric outer-measure construction with gauge r↦r^a and no dimensional prefactor, taking values in ℝ≥0∞.

binders.type: emetric space with its Borel measurable structure

definitions.type: Hausdorff dimension of a subset of an emetric space
definitions.definition: For an emetric space W and B⊆W, dimH(B)=sup{d∈ℝ≥0 : H^d(B)=∞}, interpreted in ℝ≥0∞, using the Borel structure of W. This is Hausdorff dimension and gives dimH(∅)=0. A finite dimension can be represented by its nonnegative real value; we explicitly establish finiteness before doing so.
I=[0,1], the closed unit interval in ℝ.
For a metric space W, MaxProd(W)=W×ℝ with distance max(dist(x,y),|t-u|) between (x,t) and (y,u). For real normed W this is its usual maximum product norm.

definitions.type: family of real normed spaces indexed by natural numbers
definitions.definition: L2Prod(m)=WithLp 2 (Rn(m)×ℝ), with the library L² product norm and its induced metric.
For every natural m, euclideanLift m=WithLp.toLp 2 on Rn(m)×ℝ; it is the identity on underlying pairs. This is exactly the definition in the frozen basis header.

definitions.type: family of coordinate concatenation maps L2Prod(m)→Rn(m+1)
definitions.definition: For each natural m, j(m)(p) is the (m+1)-tuple whose first m coordinates are those of p.fst and whose last coordinate is p.snd. This defines a total coordinate concatenation map.
F=E×I, regarded during the cover argument as a subset of MaxProd(Rn(n₀)).
D=dimH(E), with E in its original Euclidean Rn(n₀) metric.
T=dimH(F), using the maximum product metric.
G consists of coordinate concatenations (x_0,…,x_{n₀-1},t) with x∈E and t∈I. This is exactly E×[0,1] under the original target's specified identification with Euclidean ℝ^(n₀+1).

definitions.type: Lebesgue measure on the real line
definitions.definition: volume denotes Lebesgue measure on the Borel measurable space ℝ, with values in ℝ≥0∞.

definitions.type: set indicator with a zero outside branch
definitions.definition: For a set B⊆W and function f:W→ℝ≥0∞, indicator(B,f)(t)=f(t) for t∈B and 0 otherwise. We write 1_B(t)c for indicator(B,constant c)(t), including c=∞; this uses a zero branch outside B.

source.source_statement:
For every n≥0 and every S⊆Rn(n)×ℝ equipped with the maximum product norm, euclideanLift n sends S to an equal-dimensional set in WithLp 2 (Rn(n)×ℝ). This is the identity on underlying pairs and equips the target with the Euclidean product norm.
Closed basis type:
∀ (n : ℕ) (S : Set (BasisObjects.Rn n × ℝ)),
  dimH (BasisObjects.euclideanLift n '' S) = dimH S
Prepared proof:
intro n S
exact YuiBasis.B005 (BasisObjects.Rn n × ℝ) (WithLp 2 (BasisObjects.Rn n × ℝ))
  (WithLp.prodContinuousLinearEquiv 2 ℝ (BasisObjects.Rn n) ℝ).symm S
source.context: Both factors are real normed spaces. prodContinuousLinearEquiv is a continuous linear equivalence from WithLp 2 (Rn(n)×ℝ) to the ordinary maximum-norm product. Its inverse has underlying map WithLp.toLp 2. ContinuousLinearEquiv.dimH_image, with scalar field ℝ, gives the displayed equality for every set and every natural n, without original H or measurability of S. No textbook result is assumed.

propositions.statement: For every metric space X, subset A⊆X and real a>0, the positive-scale contents C^a_δ(A) are exactly the unnormalized real-diameter countable-cover contents of the original problem. Finite or countable index families can be reindexed into ℕ with empty padding and unchanged cost. For 0<δ₁≤δ₂, C^a_δ₂(A)≤C^a_δ₁(A). Each admissible δ-cover has cost at least C^a_δ(A), and every lower bound for all admissible costs bounds C^a_δ(A) below (including when no cover exists). H^a(A)=sup_{δ>0} C^a_δ(A), so C^a_δ(A)≤H^a(A). For δ>0, C^a_δ(A)=0 iff for every real ε>0 there is an admissible countable δ-cover with a-cost <ε. Consequently H^a(A)=0 iff such covers exist at every positive δ and every positive ε. All costs and infima are in ℝ≥0∞; empty members contribute zero.

propositions.statement: For every metric space X, A⊆X and real q>0, H^q(A)=0 implies H^(q+1)(A×I)=0, with A×I regarded as a subset of MaxProd(X). Under the same premises q>0 and H^q(A)=0, for every δ>0 and ε>0 there is a countable δ-cover of A×I with (q+1)-cost <ε. This includes singleton and zero-dimensional metric spaces.

For every metric space X, A⊆X, real s>0 and δ>0, C^s_δ(A)≤C^(s+1)_δ(A×I) in the maximum product metric MaxProd(X). Consequently H^s(A)≤H^(s+1)(A×I). These inequalities are in ℝ≥0∞; neither finiteness, compactness nor measurability of A or of the covering sets is required.

In particular D and T have finite nonnegative real representatives, and their orders and addition by finite numbers agree with the corresponding ℝ≥0∞ operations. These assertions include n₀=0.

The coordinate concatenation map j(n₀):L2Prod(n₀)→Rn(n₀+1) is a bijective isometry for the library L² product norm and the Euclidean norm on Rn(n₀+1). Its inverse truncates the first n₀ coordinates and extracts the last coordinate. It sends euclideanLift n₀ '' F exactly to G. For any x,y∈Rn(n₀) and t,u∈ℝ, the squared distance of the concatenated points is Σ_{h<n₀}|x_h-y_h|²+|t-u|², equal to the squared L² product distance between euclideanLift n₀ (x,t) and euclideanLift n₀ (y,u). For n₀=0 the sum is empty and this is the usual identification of ℝ^0×ℝ with ℝ.

Fix A⊆X.
Fix real a; temporarily assume L1: a>0.
Fix an arbitrary real scale δ; positive-scale uses are under the stated local antecedents.
Fix an arbitrary real tolerance ε; positivity is the local antecedent in S002.
In the extended-scale comparison let r range over positive extended scales; its finite and infinite cases are treated explicitly.
For the scale-monotonicity proof fix any real δ₁.
For the scale-monotonicity proof fix any real δ₂.

argument.text: Fix X,A,a and assume L1: a>0. Work with X's Borel structure, so M001 applies and gives H^a(A)=sup_{r>0} content(a,r,A) over extended nonnegative r. For arbitrary δ, temporarily assume L2: δ>0. At the finite scale ofReal δ, every admissible covering member has finite extended diameter, hence is bounded and has ediam equal to its real diameter cast to ℝ≥0∞. The nonemptiness-proof supremum in D004 is the displayed diameter power on a nonempty member and is zero on an empty member. For a>0 this agrees with assigning the empty member diameter zero and 0^a=0. Thus the nested infima are exactly the original admissible-cover infimum, with no prefactor. A finite family can be padded by empty sets. For an arbitrary countable index type choose an injection into ℕ; at each image index put the unique original member and elsewhere put ∅. This preserves the union and all nonnegative sums. Conversely an ℕ-family is countable. Discharge L2 after this finite-scale interpretation, retaining its δ>0 antecedent for every δ. For arbitrary δ₁,δ₂, temporarily assume L3: 0<δ₁≤δ₂. Every δ₁-cover is a δ₂-cover, so C^a_δ₂(A)≤C^a_δ₁(A). Discharge L3 and quantify the two scales. Every cost bounds its infimum above; a lower bound on every admissible cost bounds the infimum below. If the admissible family is empty its infimum is ∞, and the latter assertion remains true. For any positive extended scale r, if it is finite it is the cast of a positive real scale. The content at r=∞ is at most that at any fixed finite positive scale, since every finite-scale cover is also an ∞-cover. Hence the ∞ scale adds nothing to the supremum. We have proved H^a(A)=sup_{δ>0}C^a_δ(A), and each such content is ≤H^a(A).

produces.statement: Under a>0, the contents have the real-diameter countable-cover interpretation with empty padding/reindexing; they are nonincreasing in positive scale, satisfy the two infimum bounds, and H^a(A)=sup_{δ_bound>0}C^a_{δ_bound}(A).

argument.text: For the arbitrary δ,ε, temporarily assume L4: δ>0 and ε>0. Suppose L5: C^a_δ(A)=0. if every admissible cost were ≥ε, the lower-bound property in F001 would imply C^a_δ(A)≥ε>0, a contradiction. Thus an admissible cover of cost <ε exists. Discharge L5 to obtain the forward implication. In terms of the nested infima in D004, any failed cover or diameter condition has value ∞ and cannot give a value <ε, so the approximation provides an actual admissible family. Conversely assume L6: for every positive tolerance there exists an admissible cover of smaller cost. This forces the nonnegative content to be zero: a positive value, finite or infinite, has some positive finite real below it, contradicting the upper bound by those costs. Discharge L6, then L4, and quantify the arbitrary positive scale and tolerance. This proves the zero-content approximation equivalence for every positive scale. These arguments also cover an empty admissible family, whose content is ∞.

produces.statement: For every δ_bound>0, C^a_{δ_bound}(A)=0 iff at every positive finite real tolerance there exists an admissible countable δ_bound-cover of A of smaller a-cost.

argument.text: By F001, H^a(A)=0 implies each positive-scale content is zero; F002 then gives the required arbitrarily small covers at every scale. Conversely, those covers make every positive-scale content zero by F002, and their supremum is zero by F001. This proves the full equivalence and all asserted content properties. Discharge L1 to retain a>0 as an antecedent and universally quantify X,A,a and the scale/tolerance variables. No boundedness or measurability assumption on A is used.

applications.bindings: Take W=X with its Borel structure, exponent a and set A; expand the extended-scale content exactly as D004.
hypothesis_checks: The fixed X is a metric space, hence an emetric space, and we explicitly chose its Borel measurable structure.

locals.type: metric space with its Borel structure
locals.declaration: Fix an arbitrary metric space X.
Fix A⊆X.
Fix real q, under L1: q>0 and H^q(A)=0.
Fix a target scale δ, with its positivity in L2.
Fix a tolerance ε, with its positivity in L2.
Put r=min(1,δ).
Choose the admissible r-cover U supplied by F001, with Σ diam(U_i)^q<ε/4.
Set d_i=diam(U_i), which is defined since U is a finite-scale cover.
Set r_seq(i)=max(d_i,a_seq(i)). Write r_i for r_seq(i).
For each natural i put N_seq(i)=ceil(1/r_seq(i)); write N_i for this integer.

locals.type: countable family of subsets of MaxProd(X)
locals.declaration: For natural i and 0≤h<N_seq(i), set W_seq(i,h)=U_i×[h/N_seq(i),(h+1)/N_seq(i)].

argument.text: Fix X,A,q and assume L1: q>0 and H^q(A)=0. Fix arbitrary real δ,ε and assume L2: δ>0 and ε>0. Put r=min(1,δ), so 0<r≤1 and r≤δ. By N001 with exponent q, scale r and tolerance ε/4 there exists a countable r-cover U of A whose total q-cost is <ε/4; reindex it as a sequence with empty padding if necessary. In particular its members have finite diameter.

produces.statement: There exists a sequence U_bound of subsets of X covering A such that diam(U_bound(i))≤r for every natural i and Σ_i diam(U_bound(i))^q<ε/4.

argument.text: Choose U from F001 and put d_i=diam(U_i), with d_i=0 on empty members. For each natural i define a_seq(i)=min(r,(ε·2^(-i-3))^(1/q)). Both entries of this minimum are positive, so 0<a_seq(i)≤r and a_seq(i)^q≤ε·2^(-i-3). The nonnegative geometric series has sum Σ_{i≥0}2^(-i-3)=1/4 (its partial sums are (1/4)(1-2^(-m)) for the first m terms). Hence Σ a_seq(i)^q≤ε/4. Put r_i=max(d_i,a_seq(i)). Then 0<r_i≤r≤1 and r_i^q=max(d_i^q,a_seq(i)^q)≤d_i^q+a_seq(i)^q. Summing nonnegative terms, using F001 and the geometric bound, gives Σ r_i^q<ε/2. Numerical padding changes no covering set and works even if X is a singleton.

produces.statement: U covers A, d_i=diam(U_i)≤r_i, and 0<r_i≤r≤min(1,δ) for all natural i; Σ_i r_i^q<ε/2.

argument.text: For each natural i put N_i=ceil(1/r_i), a positive integer. Then 1/N_i≤r_i and N_i≤1/r_i+1≤2/r_i, since 0<r_i≤1. The closed intervals [h/N_i,(h+1)/N_i], 0≤h<N_i, cover I. Define W_seq(i,h)=U_i×[h/N_i,(h+1)/N_i]. In the maximum product metric any two points of this product have distance at most r_i, since the first-coordinate diameter is d_i≤r_i and the second-coordinate interval length is 1/N_i≤r_i. The product family covers A×I, and its index set {(i,h):i∈ℕ,0≤h<N_i} is countable. Empty products have zero cost. By N001 this countable family may be reindexed into ℕ without changing the union or sum. It is a δ-cover, and its total (q+1)-cost is at most Σ_i N_i r_i^(q+1)≤2Σ_i r_i^q<ε. The power cancellation r_i^(q+1)/r_i=r_i^q is valid because r_i>0. Rearranging these nonnegative sums is legitimate, and the upper bound is finite.

produces.statement: There exists a countable δ-cover of A×I in MaxProd(X) with total (q+1)-cost <ε.

argument.text: F003 holds for arbitrary positive δ,ε. Discharge L2 to obtain existence of the stated arbitrarily fine arbitrarily cheap covers. Since q+1>0, N001, now for MaxProd(X), A×I and exponent q+1, implies H^(q+1)(A×I)=0. Discharge L1 and universally quantify X,A,q. This proves the output proposition on the whole asserted domain without any positive-diameter assumption on the covering sets.

locals.type: metric space with its Borel structure
locals.declaration: Fix an arbitrary metric space X.
Fix any A⊆X.
Fix real s with positivity in L1.
Fix real scale δ with positivity in L1.
Set c=C^s_δ(A), allowing c=∞.
Take any sequence V; under L2 assume it covers A×I and has each diameter ≤δ.
Write ρ_i=rho(i)=diam(V_i), with value zero on empty members.
A_seq(i)=π_X(V_i), written A_i.
B_seq(i)=π_ℝ(V_i), written B_i.
Put J_i=[inf B_i,sup B_i] for nonempty V_i and J_i=∅ for empty V_i. The infimum/supremum are of bounded nonempty sets, as proved in S001.
Set f_seq(i)(t)=1_{I∩J_seq(i)}(t) rho(i)^s.
Set g(t)=1_I(t)c, with the zero indicator branch outside I.
Fix an arbitrary real t in the pointwise proof.
For the coverage verification fix any x∈X; membership in A is the temporary antecedent L4.

argument.text: Fix X,A,s,δ and assume L1: s>0 and δ>0. Set c=C^s_δ(A), possibly ∞. Take any sequence V and assume L2: V is a δ-cover of A×I in MaxProd(X). Put ρ_i=diam(V_i), A_i=π_X(V_i), B_i=π_ℝ(V_i). Every V_i is bounded, since its extended diameter is ≤δ<∞. Each projection has pairwise distances at most ρ_i, whence diam A_i≤ρ_i and diam B_i≤ρ_i≤δ. For a nonempty V_i, B_i is nonempty and bounded above and below: choose any one of its points and use the finite diameter bound. Thus inf B_i and sup B_i exist as real numbers. Put J_i=[inf B_i,sup B_i]. The least-upper-bound and greatest-lower-bound properties give B_i⊆J_i and sup B_i-inf B_i≤ρ_i: for every b,b'∈B_i one has b-b'≤ρ_i, and taking supremum in b then infimum in b' preserves the inequality. In particular inf B_i≤sup B_i. For empty V_i put ρ_i=0 and A_i=B_i=J_i=∅. Each J_i is a closed real interval or ∅, hence Borel measurable, and all projection bounds remain valid. This construction imposes no measurability on V_i or its projections.

produces.statement: For every natural i, A_i=π_X(V_i), B_i=π_ℝ(V_i), B_i⊆J_i, diam(A_i)≤ρ_i≤δ, and J_i is Borel measurable; for nonempty V_i it is [inf B_i,sup B_i] with 0≤sup B_i-inf B_i≤ρ_i, and for empty V_i all these sets are empty and ρ_i=0.

argument.text: For each nonempty member, apply M009 with endpoints inf B_i and sup B_i. By F001, volume(J_i)=ofReal(sup B_i-inf B_i)≤ρ_i. For an empty member volume(J_i)=volume(∅)=0=ρ_i by the empty-set axiom of a measure. Also I=[0,1] is closed and measurable and M009 with endpoints 0,1 gives volume(I)=1. Since I∩J_i⊆J_i, measure monotonicity gives volume(I∩J_i)≤volume(J_i)≤ρ_i; each intersection is measurable as an intersection of closed measurable sets.

produces.statement: I and every I∩J_i are Borel measurable, volume(I)=1, and volume(I∩J_i)≤volume(J_i)≤ρ_i for every natural i.

argument.text: Define g(t)=1_I(t)c and f_seq(i)(t)=1_{I∩J_i}(t)ρ_i^s. Fix any real t. In the case L3: t∈I, the family consisting of A_i when t∈J_i and ∅ otherwise covers A: under the auxiliary antecedent L4: x∈A, L2 supplies an i with (x,t)∈V_i, so x∈A_i and t∈B_i⊆J_i. This proves membership in the projected union; discharge L4 and quantify x. Each such projected set has diameter ≤ρ_i≤δ by F001. N001 therefore gives c≤Σ_i ρ_i^s 1_{J_i}(t)=Σ_i f_seq(i)(t). Discharge L3 after the inside-I argument. If t∉I, g(t)=0 and every f_seq(i)(t)=0 by the indicator zero branch, so the same inequality holds. Universal introduction in t gives g≤Σ_i f_seq(i) pointwise on ℝ, also if c=∞. F002 shows that every indicator summand is Borel measurable: its only values are a nonnegative constant and zero on complementary measurable pieces, hence it is also volume-almost-everywhere measurable. No product of an undefined infinite real quantity is used.

produces.statement: g≤(t↦Σ_i f_seq(i)(t)) pointwise on ℝ, and every f_seq(i) is volume-almost-everywhere measurable, with g=1_I c and f_seq(i)=1_{I∩J_i}ρ_i^s.

argument.text:
Integrate F003 over ℝ with Lebesgue measure. M011 gives lintegral(volume,g)≤lintegral(volume,Σ_i f_seq(i)). M012 for I and constant c, together with volume(I)=1 from F002, gives lintegral(volume,g)=c·1=c, even when c=∞. M010 for the countable family f_seq exchanges the nonnegative series and lower integral, since F003 established almost-everywhere measurability of each summand. M012 for I∩J_i and constant ρ_i^s evaluates each term. Thus
c=c·volume(I)
 ≤Σ_i ρ_i^s volume(I∩J_i)
 ≤Σ_i ρ_i^s volume(J_i)
 ≤Σ_i ρ_i^s ρ_i
 =Σ_i ρ_i^(s+1).
The middle bounds use F002 and monotonicity of multiplication and nonnegative sums. Each ρ_i is finite and nonnegative, and ρ_i^s·ρ_i=ρ_i^(s+1) holds for positive ρ_i by the real-power law and for ρ_i=0 because s>0. This is an ℝ≥0∞ computation; neither c nor the series need be finite. Discharge L2: every admissible δ-cover has (s+1)-cost at least c.

produces.statement: Every admissible countable δ-cover of A×I in MaxProd(X) has total (s+1)-cost at least c=C^s_δ(A).

argument.text: By the lower-infimum bound in N001, F004 implies C^s_δ(A)≤C^(s+1)_δ(A×I), including if no admissible product cover exists. This holds at every δ>0. Taking suprema over positive scales and using N001 for both positive exponents s and s+1 gives H^s(A)≤H^(s+1)(A×I). Discharge L1 and universally quantify X,A,s and the scale. These are the complete scale and measure inequalities asserted in the output proposition.

applications.bindings: For each nonempty V_i set a=inf B_i,b=sup B_i; also set a=0,b=1 for I.
Take W=ℝ with its Borel structure, μ=volume, f=g and the source upper function equal to t↦Σ_i f_seq(i)(t).
hypothesis_checks: ℝ is a measurable Borel space and volume is Lebesgue measure.
F003 proves this pointwise inequality on all of ℝ, including outside I.

applications.bindings: Take W=ℝ, μ=volume, J=ℕ, and the source family f=f_seq.
hypothesis_checks: ℝ has its Borel measurable structure and volume is a measure.
ℕ is countable.
F003 proves each f_seq(i) measurable, hence volume-almost-everywhere measurable.

applications.bindings: Take W=ℝ, μ=volume, B=I and constant c=C^s_δ(A).
hypothesis_checks: ℝ with its Borel structure and Lebesgue volume is a measured space.
F002 states that I is measurable.

applications.bindings: For every natural i take W=ℝ, μ=volume, B=I∩J_i and the nonnegative constant ρ_i^s.
hypothesis_checks: ℝ with its Borel structure and Lebesgue volume is a measured space.
F002 states that every I∩J_i is measurable.

locals.type: family of vectors of Rn(n₀) indexed by h<n₀
locals.declaration: Define e_basis(h), written e_h, to have coordinate 1 at h and 0 at every other coordinate.
Choose x_f∈E by H001.
Define f_f(t)=(x_f,t).
In the distance-preservation calculation fix arbitrary real t.
In the distance-preservation calculation fix arbitrary real u.

argument.text: Define e_h=e_basis(h) by the standard coordinate formula: its h-th coordinate is 1 and every other coordinate is 0. The n₀ coordinate unit vectors form a real basis of Rn(n₀): every vector is its finite coordinate linear combination, and equality of coordinates forces all coefficients in a zero combination to vanish. There are n₀ vectors. For n₀=0 this is the empty basis of the zero vector space. In MaxProd(Rn(n₀)), the n₀ vectors (e_h,0) together with (0,1) similarly span uniquely, by the first coordinates and last coordinate, so its real dimension is n₀+1. Both are real normed vector spaces (the second with the maximum product norm) and finite dimensional. Apply M007 to their full spaces and M006 to E⊆univ Rn(n₀) and F⊆univ MaxProd(Rn(n₀)). We obtain 0≤D≤n₀ and 0≤T≤n₀+1. The lower zero bounds follow from the ℝ≥0∞ codomain of dimH. Thus D and T are finite, including when n₀=0. A finite extended nonnegative real is the cast of its unique nonnegative real representative, and casts preserve finite sums and order.

produces.statement: 0≤D≤n₀<∞ and 0≤T≤n₀+1<∞; both dimensions have nonnegative real representatives with the same finite order and addition.

argument.text: The real line has basis {1}, hence real dimension one. The set I=[0,1] contains the open interval (0,1) in its interior: for each of its points the distance to the two endpoints has a positive minimum, giving a contained open ball. In particular 1/2 belongs to the interior. Apply M013 to the real normed space ℝ and A=I. Its hypotheses hold and it gives dimH(I)=1.

produces.statement: dimH(I)=1.

argument.text: H001 supplies x_f∈E. Define f_f(t)=(x_f,t). For any real t,u, the maximum product distance between f_f(t) and f_f(u) is max(dist(x_f,x_f),|t-u|)=|t-u|. Thus f_f is an isometry; its image of I is {x_f}×I, a subset of F by x_f∈E.

produces.statement: f_f:ℝ→MaxProd(Rn(n₀)) is an isometry and f_f '' I⊆F.

argument.text: Apply M008 to f_f and I, using the isometry in F003. It gives dimH(f_f '' I)=dimH(I)=1 by F002. Apply M006 to f_f '' I⊆F, also in F003, to get 1≤dimH(F)=T. Combining with F001 proves 0≤D≤n₀<∞ and 1≤T≤n₀+1<∞, together with dimH(I)=1 and the finite real identifications. The chosen point and its map do not occur in the output proposition.

hypothesis_checks: Both are real normed vector spaces by D001 and D009.
S001 displays bases of size n₀ and n₀+1, including the empty basis for Rn(0).

applications.bindings: Take W=Rn(n₀), A=E,B=univ; then W=MaxProd(Rn(n₀)), A=F,B=univ.
hypothesis_checks: Each normed space is a metric, hence emetric space.
Every set is contained in its full ambient space.
ℝ has its usual real normed vector-space structure.
The singleton basis {1} spans ℝ and is linearly independent.
S002 proves (0,1)⊆interior I and exhibits the point 1/2.

applications.bindings: Take W=ℝ, Z=MaxProd(Rn(n₀)), f=f_f and A=I.
hypothesis_checks: The real line and the maximum product are metric, hence emetric spaces.
F003 proves distance preservation; finite real distances give extended distance preservation as well.

applications.bindings: Take W=MaxProd(Rn(n₀)), A=f_f '' I and B=F.
hypothesis_checks: The maximum product is a metric, hence emetric space.
F003 exports the required image inclusion.

locals.declaration: Let d_real be the finite real representative of D from N004.
Let k_real be the finite real representative of T from N004.
Fix arbitrary real q; the condition q>d_real is the local antecedent L1.
Under L2 put q_mid=(d_real+k_real-1)/2.

argument.text: By N004, write D and T as casts of finite real values d_real≥0 and k_real≥1, respectively. Order and addition of these finite values agree with their real operations.

produces.statement: D is the cast of d_real≥0, T is the cast of k_real≥1, and the casts preserve their finite order and addition.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary real q and assume L1: q>d_real. F001 gives q>0, so q defines a nonnegative real exponent. M003 with set E and exponent q gives H^q(E)=0, since dimH(E)=D<q. Apply N002 to X=Rn(n₀), A=E and q. Its positive-exponent and zero-measure premises have just been established, and E×I in MaxProd(Rn(n₀)) is F. Therefore H^(q+1)(F)=0.

Since q+1>0, it is also a nonnegative real exponent. By F002 its Hausdorff measure on F is zero, hence different from ∞. Apply M004 with F and exponent q+1. It gives T≤q+1, equivalently k_real≤q+1 by F001. Discharge L1: for every real q>d_real one has k_real≤q+1.

produces.statement: For every real q_bound>d_real, k_real≤q_bound+1.

argument.text: Assume for contradiction L2: k_real>d_real+1. Put q_mid=(d_real+k_real-1)/2. Then d_real<q_mid<k_real-1, because k_real-1>d_real. F003 with q=q_mid gives k_real≤q_mid+1<k_real, a contradiction. Discharge L2 to obtain k_real≤d_real+1. Cast back by F001: T≤D+1. Finiteness is already supplied by F001. This proves the output proposition for every natural n₀, including zero.

applications.bindings: Take W=Rn(n₀) with its Borel structure, A=E and source nonnegative exponent d equal to q.
hypothesis_checks: Rn(n₀) is a Euclidean metric space and is equipped with its Borel structure.
F001 and L1 give q>d_real≥0.
D=dimH(E) is the cast of d_real by F001, so L1 gives dimH(E)<q.

applications.bindings: Take W=MaxProd(Rn(n₀)) with its Borel structure, A=F and source exponent d=q+1.
hypothesis_checks: The maximum product is a metric space with its Borel structure.
F002 gives q>0, hence q+1>0.
F002 gives H^(q+1)(F)=0 and zero is different from ∞.

locals.declaration: Let d_real be the finite nonnegative real representative of D given by N004.
Let k_real be the finite real representative of T given by N004.
Under L1,L2 set s_mid=(k_real-1+d_real)/2.

argument.text: By N004 write D,T as casts of real values d_real≥0 and k_real≥1. Their orders and addition agree with real operations. If L3: d_real=0, the fibre bound k_real≥1 gives k_real≥d_real+1. Discharge L3 to retain this implication. Since d_real≥0, the other case is d_real>0.

produces.statement: D and T are the casts of d_real≥0 and k_real≥1 with compatible order and addition, and d_real=0 implies k_real≥d_real+1.

argument.text: Assume L1: d_real>0. To prove the lower bound, assume for contradiction L2: k_real<d_real+1. Then 0≤k_real-1<d_real by F001. Put s_mid=(k_real-1+d_real)/2. These inequalities imply 0<s_mid<d_real and k_real<s_mid+1. The strict positivity of s_mid follows from d_real>0 even if k_real-1=0.

produces.statement: 0<s_mid<d_real and k_real<s_mid+1.

argument.text: By F002, M002 applied to E at the nonnegative exponent s_mid gives H^s_mid(E)=∞, because dimH(E)=D is the cast of d_real. N003, applied with X=Rn(n₀), A=E and s=s_mid, gives H^s_mid(E)≤H^(s_mid+1)(F). Consequently H^(s_mid+1)(F)=∞.

M005 with A=F and the nonnegative exponent s_mid+1 yields s_mid+1≤T from F003, equivalently s_mid+1≤k_real by F001. This contradicts F002. Discharge L2 and conclude k_real≥d_real+1 under L1. Discharge L1, and combine with the d_real=0 implication in F001 by exhaustive cases on d_real≥0. Hence k_real≥d_real+1 for all cases.

produces.statement: k_real≥d_real+1, equivalently T≥D+1.

argument.text: F004 gives T≥D+1, and N005 gives T≤D+1. Antisymmetry proves T=D+1. Both dimensions and their sum are finite by F001 and N004. When n₀=0, N004 forces D=0 and the fibre branch already supplies the lower bound; the upper proof also covered this case. This proves the output proposition. Compactness remains an original hypothesis in the global specification, although this replacement proof does not use it.

applications.bindings: Take W=Rn(n₀) with its Borel structure, A=E, and the nonnegative exponent d=s_mid.
hypothesis_checks: Rn(n₀) is Euclidean and equipped with its Borel structure.
F002 establishes s_mid>0.
F001 identifies dimH(E)=D with d_real and F002 gives s_mid<d_real.

applications.bindings: Take W=MaxProd(Rn(n₀)) with its Borel structure, A=F and exponent d=s_mid+1.
hypothesis_checks: The maximum product is a metric space with its Borel structure.
F002 gives s_mid>0, hence s_mid+1≥0.
F003, proved in S003 from M002 and N003, states H^(s_mid+1)(F)=∞.

locals.declaration: Fix arbitrary p∈L2Prod(n₀).
Fix arbitrary z∈L2Prod(n₀).
For the inverse construction take any v∈Rn(n₀+1).
For the final squared-distance specialization fix arbitrary x of the declared type.
For the final squared-distance specialization fix arbitrary y of the declared type.
For the final squared-distance specialization fix arbitrary t of the declared type.
For the final squared-distance specialization fix arbitrary u of the declared type.

argument.text:
Fix arbitrary p,z∈L2Prod(n₀). Apply M014 with W=Rn(n₀), Z=ℝ and argument p-z. These are normed additive commutative groups, hence satisfy its seminormed assumptions. With the coordinatewise subtraction and distance as norm of difference, the source gives
 dist(p,z)²=‖p.fst-z.fst‖²+|p.snd-z.snd|²
 =Σ_{h<n₀}|p.fst_h-z.fst_h|²+|p.snd-z.snd|².
The second equality uses the defining squared Euclidean norm on Rn(n₀). On the other hand, the defining squared norm on Rn(n₀+1), split into its first n₀ coordinates and last coordinate, gives
 dist(j(n₀)(p),j(n₀)(z))²=Σ_{h<n₀}|p.fst_h-z.fst_h|²+|p.snd-z.snd|².
The two nonnegative distances have equal squares; hence they are equal. These formulas hold also when n₀=0, with an empty finite sum.

produces.statement: For all p_bound,z_bound∈L2Prod(n₀), dist(j(n₀)(p_bound),j(n₀)(z_bound))=dist(p_bound,z_bound), and their common square is Σ_{h<n₀}|p_bound.fst_h-z_bound.fst_h|²+|p_bound.snd-z_bound.snd|².

argument.text: By F001, j(n₀) is an isometry. Its explicit inverse sends a vector v∈Rn(n₀+1) to the pair consisting of its first n₀ coordinates in Rn(n₀) and its last coordinate, regarded as an element of L2Prod(n₀) using euclideanLift n₀. Coordinate evaluation shows that both composites are the identity. Hence j(n₀) is bijective. By the definitions of F,G,euclideanLift and j, a point of j(n₀) '' (euclideanLift n₀ '' F) is precisely a concatenation of x∈E and t∈I; conversely every such concatenation arises this way. Thus this image equals G. For arbitrary x,y∈Rn(n₀) and real t,u, specialize F001 with p_bound=euclideanLift n₀ (x,t) and z_bound=euclideanLift n₀ (y,u) to obtain the squared-distance formula stated in the output proposition for every such x,y,t,u. For n₀=0 the inverse still extracts the last coordinate and the empty initial tuple; every step is unchanged.

applications.bindings: Take the two source groups to be Rn(n₀) and ℝ and source point p equal to the current difference p-z∈L2Prod(n₀).
hypothesis_checks: Rn(n₀) and ℝ are real normed additive commutative groups, hence seminormed additive commutative groups.

argument.text: Apply the exact prepared basis port E001 with its universally bound n equal to the current n₀ and S=F⊆MaxProd(Rn(n₀)). Its identity map on underlying pairs is euclideanLift n₀, with image in L2Prod(n₀). It gives dimH(euclideanLift n₀ '' F)=dimH(F)=T. This is exactly the registered maximum-to-L² product dimension equality.

produces.statement: dimH(euclideanLift n₀ '' F)=T.

argument.text: N007 proves that j(n₀):L2Prod(n₀)→Rn(n₀+1) is an isometry and that j(n₀) '' (euclideanLift n₀ '' F)=G. Apply M008 with this map and set euclideanLift n₀ '' F. It gives dimH(G)=dimH(euclideanLift n₀ '' F). By F001 and N006 this equals T=D+1=dimH(E)+1. N006 also provides finiteness. By D016, G is exactly the specified Euclidean E×[0,1] under coordinate concatenation, and E on the right retains its original Euclidean Rn(n₀) metric. N007 includes the n₀=0 identification, so there is no excluded ambient dimension. Since the dimensions are finite, the extended nonnegative equality is also equality of the real Hausdorff dimensions.
